Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity guardrail ask (HLX)

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our model roadmap has accelerated and we want to lock in a reserved pool, but procurement is asking for pricing protections tied to GPU market swings. Specifically Helix needs: a short-term floor or index cushion if market spot rates rise >20% during the first 12 months. Can Redwood provide an indexed guardrail (e.g., GPU-price cushion + defined discount tiers) or a short re-opener window to reprice?

We'd like to close commercial terms by end of May. Attaching our proforma numbers so you can see expected consumption.

Attachments: HLX_proforma_v3.xlsx

Best,
Sara Mills
Head of Procurement, Helix Therapeutics
procurement@helixthera.com

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity guardrail ask (HLX)

Sara —

Appreciate the proforma. High level options we can take back to pricing:

1) Fixed floor + quarterly indexation window: 9-month firm floor, then quarterly review tied to a lightweight GPU index (up/down triggers at +/- 15%).
2) Tiered discount band: deeper discount up to commit volume; partial protection above a defined threshold with a blended pass-through.
3) Short re-opener clause: 3-month review window if spot market moves >20% for 60 consecutive days.

I cc'ed Marissa (finance) and Marcus (sales ops) to weigh the margin sensitivity and approval path. Can you confirm which of the three approaches is closest to what Helix needs (firm floor vs re-opener vs tiered)?

Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 13:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity guardrail ask (HLX) — Pricing sensitivity

Team —

Quick notes from finance: we modeled the three options against current SKU mix and two downside GPU scenarios (15% and 30% price shock). Results:

- Option 1 (9m floor + quarterly index): Risk to margin at 30% shock is significant beyond month 9. Approve with a limited escalation cap (e.g., price pass-through for >25% moves above baseline).
- Option 2 (Tiered discounts): Most flexible; keeps unit economics intact if we can structure tiers tied to committed vs burst usage.
- Option 3 (3m re-opener): Operationally simpler but leaves us exposed if market moves quickly.

I've uploaded a short spreadsheet with scenario outputs. Attaching a draft of the indexation clause we typically include (gpu-indexation-term-draft.pdf).

Next step: need legal to review the clause language and a product confirmation on how prefix caching/auto-burst will be treated for committed vs burst tokens. Kimberly, can you take point on the clause language review? Marcus, can you confirm expected SKU mix for HLX?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Karthik / Sara —

Helix preference is Option 1 or a close variant: a firm 12-month floor with a mid-term review at month 6 (not just quarterly). The ask is driven by our board — they need a clear protection in case GPU supply tightens. If Redwood can accept a 12-month floor with an explicit re-open at month 6 (limited to price index repricing and capped at X% per quarter), we can get internal approval faster.

We're okay with a small pass-through above a capped threshold but want predictability on our unit cost for budgeting.

-David

Folks —

Helix is asking for 12-month floor + a 6-month re-open for indexation with a capped pass-through. Quick ask:
- Marissa: what is the maximum discount we can sustain at the commit volume if we accept 12m firm floor (scenario: 25% GPU cost spike)?
- Marcus: confirm SKU mix & expected burst % (they've signaled 20% burst above committed).
- Kimberly: can legal draft a limited re-opener clause that limits repricing to +/- 10% per quarter and includes an escape if market moves >40% in a 30-day window?

Attaching the HLX Mutual Action Plan they sent. We need to respond to Helix with an offer that balances predictability and our margin protection. I recommend: 12-month floor, 6-month review, capped pass-through starting at +20% index move, and an exec approval path for anything beyond +35%.

Thanks,
Karthik

Subject: Re: Internal: HLX guardrail negotiation — Legal signoff route

Karthik / team —

I've drafted language that implements the 12-month firm floor with a 6-month review window. Key points:
- Repricing limited to index moves beyond +/-20% from baseline.
- Any repricing is capped at 10% per quarter and 25% cumulative in a 12-month period.
- If market moves >40% in any 30-day period, either party may call for a negotiated amendment (exec signoff required).

Finance and I recommend we pre-authorize a one-time commercial concession: up to a 7% additional discount on committed SKU up to the first 6 months (subject to exec approval) to close by 31-May. If pricing exposure exceeds the modeled 30% shock, we trigger the exec escalation.

If everyone agrees, I'll insert these clauses into the redline and send to Helix with a DocuSign link for the MSA amendment.
